action.Left:Predicted trajectories alone and overlaid on
generated videos.Right:Zero-shot real-robot rollout obtained by converting predicted
trajectories into commands with inverse kinematics.

Figure 5:Real-world hardware platform.A 7-DoF Franka Research 3 robot arm equipped with a Robotiq 2F-85 gripper and a wrist-mounted Zed Mini stereo camera.
Two external Zed 2i stereo cameras (view 1 and view 2) observe the workspace from different viewpoints, providing synchronized multi-view observations.
Figure 6:Examples of the robot manipulation tasks.

Figure 7:From predicted point trajectories to joint-space actions.Predicted 2D trajectories from both views are lifted to 3D (Stage 1) and converted into a joint trajectory by fitting the robot’s kinematic model to the lifted points (Stage 2).

Figure 9:Data scalability.FVD (top) andδavg3D\delta^{\text{3D}}_{\text{avg}}(bottom) of VPM (V) and VPM (V+T) trained on 10K, 100K, and 600K samples. The shaded area marks the gain from point supervision.

Figure 11:Qualitative results of multi-view prediction.Predicted video with overlaid predicted point track for two-view (top) and three-view (bottom) scenes.
Conditioning frames are omitted.

Figure 12:Additional qualitative results of multi-view prediction.Predicted video with overlaid predicted point track on robot and general scenes from VP-WorldBench (Real, top) and VP-WorldBench (Sim, bottom).

Figure 13:Predicted vs. ground-truth videos.Each view shows the prediction next to the ground truth.
Conditioning frames are omitted.

Figure 14:Example rollouts of robot manipulation tasks.Successful rollouts of our policy on six tasks, shown from two exterior cameras and a wrist camera.
Rows are time steps sampled uniformly over each episode of lengthTT.
